Large language models can supply the missing explanation, but designs that also hand the model the detection give up the auditability that makes static analysis defensible. We keep detection with the analyser and give the model only the explaining. A preliminary user study with 20 participants and a workshop with 19 practitioners yielded five requirements. Guided by these we redesigned SAFE, an open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin that explains findings from any analyser reporting in the Static Analysis Results Interchange Format. It tiers explanations by demand, ties them to the reported data flow, and replaces the single-prompt backend with an agent that must consult the repository and the rule that fired before answering. A within-subjects crossover experiment with 24 participants compared the redesign against its predecessor. Perceived usability rose from 77.3 to 85.0 on the System Usability Scale. Actionability gained most among the explanation-quality items, the aspect both earlier studies flagged as weakest, and the odds of a correct remediation were 2.6 times higher. Triage accuracy and time per finding were indistinguishable, which we read as uninformative rather than as equivalence. Trust was the one measure that did not move, and the closing interviews indicate that grounding made findings easier to understand rather than easier to believe. Participants also drew a boundary no requirement anticipated, wanting the tool to find and explain while they judge and apply.

title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks

payload.title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks
payload.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts language models are cheap to run per token but expensive to hold in GPU memory, which drives the cost of serving them in production. One-shot expert compression shrinks them after a single calibration pass. Its two current state-of-the-art methods are REAP for expert pruning, which deletes the least salient experts, and REAM for expert merging, which merges them into the most salient ones. Both have been evaluated only on academic benchmarks. We compare the two on five multilingual production tasks of a web-hosting company, from classification to the generation of marketing HTML email templates, with two 30B-parameter models (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and the hybrid Mamba-attention Nemotron-3.5-Lightning) at 25% and 50% of experts removed and the same calibration data. Pruning wins: on the same rows, REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons and REAM in 2. At 25%, REAP keeps 93.6% of Qwen3-30B's generative quality and REAM 62.5%, although on benchmarks the two are within a point for the same model. The damage concentrates in the output contract rather than the content: 89.8-95.2% of each significant loss on email templates comes from hard-gate failures such as invalid JSON, broken mobile layouts and runaway generation, and most failed non-English domain descriptions copy the prompt's English opening phrase. Cross-perplexity and logit divergence, two diagnostics from the REAP paper, also track production quality, as does the rate of repetition loops; n-gram diversity does not. We close with practical guidance for compressing MoE models for production.

title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents

payload.title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents
payload.abstract: On-policy self-distillation lets a language agent act as its own Teacher by conditioning on privileged context such as skills written from its own trajectories. Its guidance, however, is weighted by how much this context shifts token likelihoods rather than by whether it improves behavior, so errors in self-written skills return through later updates. We propose environment-calibrated on-policy self-distillation, which uses environmental outcomes to decide how much to trust the Teacher's current guidance and which self-written skills to reinforce. Command-level advantages, estimated by comparing commands executed at similar observations, scale each Teacher preference and reward reflections and skills whose induced preferences favor higher-advantage commands. Without skills at inference, 3B and 7B agents reach 90.5% and 93.3% macro success on seen ALFWorld tasks and 75.5% and 80.5% success on WebShop. On unseen ALFWorld tasks, they outperform GRPO under the same protocol by 11.0 and 7.6 percentage points, respectively. In an ablation study, supervising only executable commands rather than the Actor's full response raises 3B WebShop success from 52.3% to 75.0%.

title: A Cost That Practice Accuracy Hides: Worked Solutions in Self-Generated Training Data and the Compositional Use of New Rules

payload.title: A Cost That Practice Accuracy Hides: Worked Solutions in Self-Generated Training Data and the Compositional Use of New Rules
payload.abstract: A worked solution can make self-generated training targets shorter and cheaper, but accuracy on the practiced operation may hide how well a model can reuse newly learned rules. We study this choice in a 2B-parameter reasoning model learning two invented quantitative rules. The model generates targets from a rule sheet alone or from the sheet plus a program-written worked solution; targets are accepted for final-answer correctness, and the support is removed for fine-tuning and evaluation. Training questions request forward use in one segment; composition requires sequential reuse of the same rule across two segments. After six passes, using a program-checked numerical signature, sheet-only targets lead by 24.3 percentage points (95% item-bootstrap CI 14.6-34.0) on composition in a prospective test. On unseen argument values, observed forward accuracy is identical (87.5% each), but composition accuracy is 58.3% versus 23.6%, a 34.7-point gap (25.7-43.8). An independently sampled second target-bank pair repeats the direction (+14.6 points, 2.1-26.0). Ten passes on the shorter worked-solution targets, approximately matching the domain tokens of six sheet-only passes while changing other training quantities, narrow the gap to 16.3 points (6.3-26.7) in the first bank pair and 6.2 points (-6.3 to 18.8) in the second, where the pre-specified test does not hold. At six passes each, the worked-solution policy uses fewer capture tokens and less update time, yet the trained models use 2.6 times as many generated tokens per composition success under the numerical signature (2.1 times in the second bank pair). Choosing a capture context therefore requires testing how the new rules are reused, alongside the inference cost of those uses, rather than relying on forward accuracy alone.

title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment

payload.title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment
payload.abstract: Systematic literature reviews (SRs) remain slow and labor-intensive, and most automation tools address single stages of the workflow. We present PARIS (PRISMA Agentic Research Intelligence System), an open-source framework in which a conductor agent running in Claude Code orchestrates 15 specialized large language model (LLM) agents, from scoping a research question to exporting a manuscript draft. Agents are specified declaratively, coordinate exclusively through persisted artifacts that the conductor validates before every transition, and delegate retrieval, bibliometric analysis and scoring to deterministic Python utilities. Three human checkpoints gate study inclusion, corpus adequacy and the synthesis outline. We also introduce QualityScore, a pre-synthesis index that aggregates normalized network, bibliometric, semantic and process sub-scores into a 0-100 grade. Two case studies illustrate both: AI chatbots and university students' learning (388 records, 100 included) and AI-assisted SR methods (131 records, 123 included, QualityScore 69.1 recomputed with a proxy network sub-score). They show end-to-end feasibility across domains and the diagnostic use of QualityScore: in the first run, corpus improvements chosen at the corpus-adequacy checkpoint raised the score from 74.6 to 81.9 and the number of pre-2023 studies from 1 to 19. Audits of both runs exposed failure modes: incomplete retrieval, counts that drifted between agents, unrecorded or delegated checkpoint decisions and a grade that depends on how citation data are handled. PARIS fully supports 8 of the 27 PRISMA 2020 items and partially supports 11. Output quality has so far been judged only by an internal reviewer agent; independent validation against human reviews is the next step.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Stability in Network Intrusion Detection

payload.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Stability in Network Intrusion Detection
payload.abstract: Quantum kernel methods have been proposed for network intrusion detection, yet their performance limitations are often attributed to noise in current quantum hardware. This study evaluates that assumption through a controlled analysis of Pegasos-QSVC on the NSL-KDD and ToN-IoT datasets. We perform 56 quantum experiments using one exact noiseless statevector backend and three noise-simulated superconducting backends while keeping preprocessing, PCA features, data splits, and classical baselines identical. XGBoost achieves accuracies of 98.94% on NSL-KDD and 99.41% on ToN-IoT, compared with 91.80% and 82.98% for Pegasos-QSVC. The quantum model also exhibits substantially greater seed-dependent variability. Eight runs collapse into degenerate classifiers, including four recall-collapse cases and four trivial-positive classifiers. Notably, two failures occur on the noiseless backend, demonstrating that hardware noise is not a necessary condition for classi-fier collapse. Kernel Gram matrix analysis further reveals low effective rank and severe ill-conditioning even in the absence of noise, indicating intrinsic fragility in the learned quantum representation. These results show that average accuracy alone can conceal operationally unacceptable behavior and highlight the importance of reporting worst-case performance, seed-level variability, class-specific metrics, and explicit degeneracy tests in quantum intrusion detection studies.

title: Graph-Based RL for Sequential Rendezvous Planning with Multiple Patrolling USVs

payload.title: Graph-Based RL for Sequential Rendezvous Planning with Multiple Patrolling USVs
payload.abstract: In patrol missions involving multiple unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), a designated command USV can support fleet management by sequentially rendezvousing with each patrolling USV. These operations require motion-feasible route planning and priority-aware rendezvous sequencing, with the objective of minimizing mission completion time and total tardiness relative to priority-dependent due dates. We propose a framework combining grid-based path planning, surrogate travel-time prediction, and graph-based reinforcement learning. The path planner accounts for ocean currents and approximates turn-rate constraints through multi-stage maneuvers, with path feasibility empirically validated through trajectory-tracking simulations. For rendezvous sequencing, a Feasible Transition Graph (FTG) represents candidate rendezvous events and temporally feasible transitions, enabling a graph neural network to exploit spatiotemporal rendezvous relationships for policy learning. A surrogate predicts travel times from compact current and motion features to avoid repeated path searches during FTG construction and policy training. Evaluation using grid-based path planning shows statistically significant average objective reductions of 10.5%, 3.5%, and 1.5% compared with greedy, MLP-RL, and 2-step lookahead greedy, respectively. The policy achieves these improvements while requiring approximately 1/35 of the latter's computation time. It maintains its advantage over MLP-RL under unseen priority-tier settings, with larger gains as fleet size increases.

title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next

payload.title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
payload.abstract: A sparse terminal reward tells an agent little about its steps. Much of the missing information is implicit in the environment's dynamics, because each state transition can change the conditions for success long before the reward arrives. A world model trained on real transitions can learn to predict what each action changes, but a predicted observation does not by itself show whether success has become more likely. With a binary terminal reward, PPO's critic makes this judgment by estimating the current policy's probability of success, but only for states the agent reaches. Our method, WM-PPO, elegantly brings the two together. For each action the policy samples, executed or not, the world model predicts the next observation and the critic values the predicted successor. In the policy channel, comparisons among these values give the policy auxiliary advantages; in the value channel, their mean gives the critic an auxiliary target. A shared gate weights both channels according to how reliably comparisons with similar margins predicted real outcomes earlier in training. The policy, critic and world model all learn from the agent's own interaction, with no teacher or privileged information, and only the policy is used at inference. With a comparable number of real environment steps, WM-PPO raises success from PPO's 63.5% to 87.5% on ALFWorld and from 39.3% to 52.9% on ScienceWorld. It matches the strongest PPO refinements we tested on ALFWorld and exceeds the best of them by 6.5 points on ScienceWorld. The trained policy more often completes prerequisite steps before placing an object or committing to an answer.

title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval

payload.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
payload.abstract: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. To address the challenges, we propose TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework for on-demand delivery: (1) Geo-Semantic ID splits merchant identifiers into geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes, making reachability a prediction target rather than a post-hoc filter; (2) Query-Geo Target Attention aggregates historical behaviors using the real-time query and location as dual targets, while encoding each behavior's own location into its attention key; (3) GMPO (Group Marginal Policy Optimization) rewrites advantages using a deduplicated group reward and marginal advantage within GRPO, avoiding auxiliary diversity objectives. Deployed online with a lightweight 0.1B backbone, TS-GEAR serves over 150 million queries per day in the search advertising pipeline of Taobao Shangou, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods on both HitRate and geographic validity, and achieving 3.8% gains in ad impressions and 4.2% in ad revenue.

title: Replication of Thermal Comfort Cohort Models: No Support for Improved Thermal Preference Prediction

payload.title: Replication of Thermal Comfort Cohort Models: No Support for Improved Thermal Preference Prediction
payload.abstract: Cohort comfort models (CCMs) aim to overcome the extensive individual data requirements of personal comfort models (PCMs) by grouping occupants based on demographic and psychometric characteristics (cold start) or similar thermal preferences (warm start). We evaluated the validity of the reported CCM performance gains through (i) a methodological assessment of the original study, (ii) a replication using one of the two original datasets (DORN: 20 participants, 6 months) under a revised experimental protocol, and (iii) a replication using an independently collected dataset (PersonAI: 72 participants, 4 weeks). Classification performance was evaluated using F1-micro, as in the original study, and F1-macro to account for class imbalance. Under F1-micro, a trivial baseline that always outputs the majority class performed on par with cohort models. Under F1-macro, all cohort models achieved lower median scores than a simple baseline that makes random predictions based on the estimated distribution of thermal preferences. In our methodological assessment we identified the following key issues: Limited data per participant and per minority class, reliance on a metric insensitive to class imbalance, missing trivial baselines, inadequate cross validation strategy, and multiple occurrences of information leakage. Our findings challenge the original study's conclusion that CCMs improve thermal preference prediction. CCMs did not outperform simple class-distribution baselines. Future studies should improve experimental designs, including controlled thermal conditions, to obtain sufficient observations across thermal preference classes.

title: Embodied First Exam

payload.title: Embodied First Exam
payload.abstract: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go beyond pick-and-place to spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. Each task can be run in up to three evaluation settings. The Standard Setting mimics the real world: the agent receives only sensor observations and, by default, cannot reset the environment. Its Realtime variant keeps the environment running while the agent reasons. The Privileged Setting gives the agent access to the full simulator state and unlimited resets, allowing it to search for an oracle solution for training purposes. Success rates in this setting serve as an approximate upper bound. On the 456 core tasks, the strongest of eight agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a success rate of 34% in the Standard Setting, leaving much room for improvement. To see where agents fail, we label the stage at which failed attempts go wrong and compare failures across agents, settings, and stage categories.

title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation

payload.title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation
payload.abstract: Robotic manipulation has advanced rapidly in mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, reliable manipulation in open-world environments requires robust spatial understanding: the ability to identify targets in complex layouts (spatial reasoning) and adapt to scenes that continuously evolve through interaction (spatial memory). Yet existing embodied benchmarks fall short in evaluating spatial understanding: they often introduce strong visual cues that bypass spatial reasoning, and focus on static scenes that offer little insight into an agent's capacity for spatial memory. To address this gap, we introduce GeoMind, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation. GeoMind comprises 54 evaluated task variants organized around spatial reasoning and spatial memory. It also incorporates a scalable pipeline that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions. Extensive evaluations across diverse embodied agents reveal their consistent weaknesses in spatial understanding. Our findings highlight that these agents struggle to track identities after spatial changes and convert relational or geometric constraints into executable actions. We release the GeoMind benchmark at https://github.com/Notfound-JH/GEOMIND-benchmark.git.

title: Transactional Data Change for Real-Time Analytics in Lakehouses

payload.title: Transactional Data Change for Real-Time Analytics in Lakehouses
payload.abstract: Real-time data analytics has become a key demand for lakehouses. It requires propagating data changes from the data source to the lakehouse in real time, while ensuring ACID guarantees and minimizing resource consumption and impact on analytical query performance. This is highly challenging for a data system according to the RUM conjecture, especially given the read-optimized immutable file storage layer in lakehouses. Existing lakehouses offer only git-style catalog version control on a single table, and they trade data freshness, query performance, and/or resource efficiency to achieve a barely acceptable data-change throughput. In this paper, we propose a novel data synchronization framework, Retina, that enables real-time, cost-efficient, query-performant, and fully transactional data changes in lakehouses. We implement and open-source Retina. Evaluations show that Retina delivers 10-millisecond-level data freshness and over 3.2 million row/s linear-scalable data-change throughput with low resource consumption and query-performance overhead, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art lakehouse systems and lake-compatible HTAP databases.

title: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception

payload.title: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception
payload.abstract: We introduce FraudBench, an evaluation of large language models' (LLMs) propensities to recommend, assist, or directly take actions that would constitute fraud under U.S. law. Our evaluation contains a novel dataset of 159 scenarios based on real-world U.S. court cases and validated by legal experts. We present each scenario to LLMs via three tasks at varying levels of autonomy: advising users, drafting messages for users to send, and acting directly on behalf of users (477 tasks total). In each scenario, FraudBench re-enacts the facts of a court case to give LLMs an opportunity, but no explicit instruction, to either misrepresent or conceal a material fact in a high-stakes commercial setting--e.g., whether to describe company-funded product testing as "independent" to customers (misrepresentation) or whether to hide unfavorable regulatory investigations from clients (concealment). We evaluate 20 LLMs across 25 experimental conditions (totaling >300,000 generations) and include a preregistered human baseline ($n_{\texttt{annotations}} = 2{,}957$, $n_{\texttt{humans}} = 996$). We score a response as fraudulent when it engages in, assists with, or recommends misrepresentation or concealment. Key findings include: (1) across LLMs, fraud rates ranged from near 0% to over 40%; (2) LLM fraud rates increased with autonomy, with overall rates of 3.0% when advising, 14.7% when drafting, and 21.4% when acting directly, without applying pressure; (3) LLMs sometimes engaged in fraud despite recognizing legal risks; (4) LLMs more often engaged in fraud by concealment than by misrepresentation; and (5) prompt-based interventions substantially affected fraud rates, with a prompt to obey the law reducing fraud rates, while prompts to maximize profits and act agentically increased fraud rates.

title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood

payload.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
payload.abstract: Code localizers are usually trained to predict the files a reference patch edits, but the code a fixer needs to read is not the same as the code it changes. We propose Fixer-Guided Localization (FGL): the localizer proposes several localizations, a frozen fixer scores each by how likely it makes a verified patch, and the localizer is trained on these scores with weighted supervised fine-tuning, without running tests and without reinforcement learning. We build the full pipeline on Gemma 4 E4B for the Kaggle Gemma-4 Developer Agent competition, from 1,629 test-verified Kimi K3 trajectories. The FGL target helps the fixer find the bug as often as the teacher's localization while using 27.5% less code. On the development set, one EM round moves the agent in the expected direction compared with a matched control: more tasks reach a patch (53 vs. 46), fewer tasks get stuck reading files that do not exist (43 vs. 54), and more tasks are solved (8 vs. 6). Training also changes how the agent works: trained agents explore about three times more than the base model and write far fewer wrong patches, and the single agent solves up to 11 of 78 tasks, against 8 for the base model. An analysis of 13 evaluation runs identifies what limits a 4B agent under an 8-minute budget (time, repetition loops and edit quality) and gives practical lessons for training small coding agents. All data, code and adapters are publicly available.

title: Beyond Flat Walks: Compositional Abstraction for Autoregressive Graph Generation

payload.title: Beyond Flat Walks: Compositional Abstraction for Autoregressive Graph Generation
payload.abstract: Autoregressive graph generators typically linearize graphs through flat node-edge walks, which can obscure higher-order structure in large and complex graphs. We introduce a hierarchical graph abstraction and coarse-to-fine generation pipeline that separates coarsening, tokenization, and decoding. This exposes three design axes: community coarsening, hierarchical tokenization, and order randomization. Across these axes, traversal-based hierarchy consistently improves distributional and structural fidelity, while its V.U.N.\ cost depends strongly on the coarsening and randomization policy. In particular, the fidelity--V.U.N.\ trade-off observed under within-community randomization is substantially reduced when traversal order is randomized across the full hierarchy. With a fixed backbone, training protocol, and matched training time across five molecular and five non-molecular benchmarks, hierarchical serialization yields consistent distributional and structural gains on all molecular datasets, while the non-molecular results further show that these gains depend on how well the supplied hierarchy aligns with structure in the target distribution. Together, these results characterize when and how hierarchical serialization benefits autoregressive graph generation.

title: DisasterVL: Evidence-Based Visual Reasoning Dataset and Model for Disaster Scene Understanding

payload.title: DisasterVL: Evidence-Based Visual Reasoning Dataset and Model for Disaster Scene Understanding
payload.abstract: We introduce DisasterVL, a dataset and benchmark for evidence-grounded reasoning about disaster imagery. It contains approximately 1.2 million images from 142 countries, paired with 25 million structured annotations covering scene captions, incident and location assessments, spatial relationships, and visual question answering (VQA). The VQA annotations link answers to visible evidence and include questions about both present and absent cues, multiple answer formats, and difficulty labels. Region-level annotations link caption phrases to bounding boxes and spatial relationships to the regions they connect. The test set contains 38,254 images spanning 75 countries and 28 hazard types. Gemini 3.1 Pro audited the test annotations, and human reviewers validated a stratified subset. On this benchmark, the 9B DisasterVLM model outperforms the evaluated general-purpose baselines on captioning, open-ended VQA, incident reasoning, and region-level grounding. Gains in text overlap are larger than gains in evidence scores. We plan to publicly release the dataset, trained models, and code.

title: Do Time-Series Foundation Models Forecast Index-Futures Returns? A Preregistered Evaluation of Models, Metrics, and Input Representations

payload.title: Do Time-Series Foundation Models Forecast Index-Futures Returns? A Preregistered Evaluation of Models, Metrics, and Input Representations
payload.abstract: We ask whether the apparent forecasting skill of frozen time-series foundation models (TSFMs) on intraday index-futures returns is incremental skill. In a pre-registered evaluation on E-mini Nasdaq-100 (NQ) and E-mini S&P 500 (ES) futures, a common panel of five zero-shot models (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Moirai 2.0 and TiRex), plus separate experiments with Kronos, is compared with a no-change forecast at 5-120 minutes, using native prices, log returns, volatility-standardised returns and a volume clock as inputs. On a blind set opened once, 0 of 160 model-representation-horizon-market cells beat no-change, and a Hansen SPA test gives p = 1.000 on both markets; a later retrospective hold-out, scored as a descriptive check, gives 0 of 120. Input representations change forecast magnitude but not accuracy, and a transformation-aware ridge regression does as well. Several standard measures nevertheless suggest skill. Price-level correlation exceeds 0.9996, but no-change scores higher. Within-day RankIC across forecast origins rewards a trivial revert-to-mean rule (+0.35 at 30 minutes); we derive the expected within-day covariance under a random walk in closed form, and a sign-randomised null reproduces about 95% of the observed value. One model beats HAR for 5-minute volatility, but not the EWMA its input already contains. On strongly planted synthetic signals the models recover part of the signal at 5 minutes, and recovery deteriorates at 30 minutes. Benchmark-level success of TSFMs should therefore not be assumed to carry over to low-signal domains such as intraday returns.

title: Visible Tails: Characterizing Adaptation to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits

payload.title: Visible Tails: Characterizing Adaptation to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits
payload.abstract: Heavy-tailed bandit learners without moment parameters face an obstruction: the rewards that carry an arm's mean can stay unseen. We address the remaining part of a COLT open problem by characterizing the optimal-arm laws that permit adaptation to unknown moments at constant-factor cost. The condition, variance-core visibility, is one-sided and translation-invariant: the mean hidden in any rare event is at most a constant multiple of the standard error of the rewards that remain. A quantile-trimmed UCB index that knows the visibility constants attains the central-moment benchmark on this class, and no single strategy adapts across all visibility levels. The same index achieves logarithmic expected regret on every instance with a visible optimal arm and finite-mean rewards. On an explicit family with no higher moment, gap $Δ$ and constant $A$, its logarithmic coefficient and the information lower bound are of order $Δ^{-1}e^{A/Δ}$, exponential in the inverse gap within one visibility class.

title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data

payload.title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
payload.abstract: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. To train the Cerebellum for natural, route-faithful motion, we develop a physics-grounded data engine that improves physical tracking of motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations. Together, these designs allow task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. In simulation, our navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls. Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 further demonstrates single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon task execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects. Project website: https://robbyant-research.github.io/LHNav/.

title: RAPA: Ray-Aware Physics Augmentation for Robust Camera-LiDAR Calibration

payload.title: RAPA: Ray-Aware Physics Augmentation for Robust Camera-LiDAR Calibration
payload.abstract: Camera-LiDAR calibration is essential for reliable perception in robotic and autonomous systems. Most target-based calibration methods rely on checkerboard observations, but accurate checkerboard feature extraction from LiDAR point clouds remains challenging due to measurement sparsity. Existing approaches either require manual annotation of 3D corners or depend on geometric feature extraction methods, both of which can become unreliable when checkerboard features are insufficiently observed. In this paper, we formulate checkerboard localization as a 2D detection problem using cylindrical LiDAR reflectivity images. To overcome the limited availability of labeled training data, we propose ray-aware physics augmentation (RAPA), which generates diverse synthetic samples from a single checkerboard observation. The generated data are used to improve detector robustness and generalization under varying sensing conditions. Across four independently captured indoor and outdoor locations, the proposed synthetic augmentation exceeds the strongest evaluated image-space augmentation baseline by 16.1-43.1 percentage points in mAP@0.5. Compared with training-free target-based methods on 242 observations, RAPA yields the largest number of valid target localizations, with 96.4% of its returned detections yielding valid target poses. These reliable localizations support downstream camera-LiDAR calibration across all four evaluated locations. Overall, RAPA addresses a key bottleneck in target-based calibration by enabling automated LiDAR-side target localization with only a single annotated target observation.

title: Toward Sustainable Agentic AI: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Iterative Self-Refinement and Tool-Augmented Coding

payload.title: Toward Sustainable Agentic AI: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Iterative Self-Refinement and Tool-Augmented Coding
payload.abstract: Agentic language model systems can improve performance either by iterating on their own outputs or by using external tools in grounded environments. While these strategies can reduce error rates and substitute for larger models in some settings, their environmental cost remains relatively underexplored. We present two complementary empirical studies that estimate the energy and carbon footprint of agentic AI across settings of increasing complexity. Study~1 evaluates iterative verbal self-refinement: GPT-4.1-mini at $k = 1$--$5$ steps versus a GPT-4.1 single-pass baseline on two MATH benchmark splits. Study~2 evaluates tool-augmented agentic coding: GPT-4.1-mini, Claude Opus~4.6, and GPT-5.3-codex on SWE-bench Lite, where agents operate inside Docker-isolated environments with access to code execution and file editing tools. In Study~1, $k=3$ refinements close a 16-percentage-point accuracy gap to within 1~point, but nearly triple the carbon footprint relative to the cheap single-pass baseline while remaining below the GPT-4.1 single-pass baseline under the current token-based carbon scenario. In Study~2, GPT-5.3-codex achieves the highest resolution rate in this sample (81.2\%), ahead of Claude Opus~4.6 (68.9\%) and GPT-4.1-mini (25.0\%), but resolved-task-normalized efficiency remains mixed: GPT-4.1-mini is lowest on estimated carbon and cost per resolved task, while GPT-5.3-codex delivers substantially higher task success. All carbon estimates cover output-token inference only; prompt tokens, which exceed 99\% of tokens in Study~2, and tool execution are not charged, so the figures are lower bounds on the full agentic footprint.

title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents

payload.title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents
payload.abstract: External tool calls are a major running cost of an LLM agent, while its training objectives align almost exclusively with task completion. In a step-level diagnosis of Qwen3.5 trajectories at two model sizes on GAIA, a long-horizon tool-use benchmark, we find that most contain removable calls, at a similar rate at both sizes. Some methods add an efficiency reward to the objective to reduce the call count, but introduce problems of their own: the anchor they price calls against is computed from the policy's own rollouts (e.g., the group's shortest correct rollout) and so moves with the policy; training can drift toward a collapsed policy that issues no tool call at all, a degeneracy seen in published reports and in our 27B baseline; and a training run delivers a single operating point, so the user cannot trade efficiency against capability. We present CARE-PO (Controllable Anchored Relative Efficiency Policy Optimization) to mitigate these problems. The efficiency reward prices calls against a reference budget anchored to the task's own difficulty and fixed before training. Injecting a successful trajectory from the training data into each online GRPO rollout group and charging for evidence a trajectory never gathers ease the drift toward a collapsed call count. Shaping the cost curve by an effort tag in the prompt yields an efficiency and a capability operating point from a single training run. On GAIA, five of the six operating points across three model sizes improve on their base model in success rate and call count at once. On four held-out multi-hop benchmarks the result is size-dependent: at 27B and 4B success rate is held or raised at a lower call count, while at 9B both operating points trade success rate for fewer calls. The call count remains well above zero throughout training at all three sizes.

title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses

payload.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
payload.abstract: AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task. To further explore these harness-side cost optimization opportunities, we analyze the cost accumulation patterns across various agent traces and identify system opportunities to reduce token use and LLM calls without modifying the model or affecting task accuracy. Based on this analysis, we design Agency, a harness interposition platform that provides a unified abstraction and allows easy and portable implementation of harness-side system optimizations on existing off-the-shelf harnesses such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Using Agency, we implement proof-of-concept optimization techniques based on our analysis and achieve cost reductions up to 35% across various real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses without compromising accuracy.

title: Joi-Bench-Task: Benchmarking Task Coordination in Full-duplex Voice Agents through Interactive Simulation

payload.title: Joi-Bench-Task: Benchmarking Task Coordination in Full-duplex Voice Agents through Interactive Simulation
payload.abstract: Full-duplex voice agents enable natural, hands-free interaction, allowing users to refine requests, redirect ongoing work, and seek clarification while the agent is speaking. However, existing voice-agent benchmarks insufficiently isolate coordination between task execution and conversation. We introduce a benchmark that assesses this coordination by examining whether agents track what is being executed, what has been completed, what has been communicated, and what remains to be reported as the conversation evolves. We propose an interactive user simulator that introduces configurable interventions at designated timing in tool execution and spoken result delivery, supporting controllable and reproducible evaluation conditions. We evaluate five leading commercial voice agents along three dimensions: execution responsiveness, coordination under request changes, and coordination under interruptions. Agent evaluations reveal persistent coordination failures. Under request changes, the highest result completion rate is only 55%, indicating difficulty for current voice agents adapting to new requests while preserving earlier obligations. After user interruption, four of the five agents exhibit average information omission rates of at least 23%. These findings highlight task coordination as a central challenge for current voice agents in complex, evolving conversations.

title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts

payload.title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts
payload.abstract: Strong machine-learning ensembles capture much of the trend, seasonality, and known events in demand, yet they can still understate peaks, miss moving events, or mistake temporary changes for shifts in demand level. We address this gap by framing forecast refinement as a reward-driven decision problem. For each forecast period, we let an agent choose among values already produced by the ensemble: its base forecast, distribution-free bounds, quantiles, and a bias-corrected estimate. We evaluate these choices against context-matched historical periods, accounting for calendar position, recurring and moving events, trend, price, and promotions. We then apply a structural seasonal guard to constrain adjustments and record the model, agent, and planner contributions to every published value. We evaluate our approach across five retail, consumer-goods, and direct-to-consumer deployments over nine months. Our refined forecasts reduce mean WMAPE by 6.3% compared with the stacked machine-learning forecast for every customer, with gains reaching 16.7%, and achieve the lowest error in 35 of 45 customer-months. Compared with statistical forecasts, our approach reduces mean error by 18.7%. These results demonstrate that context-aware, auditable action selection can add forecast value beyond a strong ensemble.

title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback

payload.title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback
payload.abstract: During reinforcement learning, experience can be both internalized in LLM parameters and retained externally as reusable textual skills. Parameter updates alter the model's behavior and the interaction experience from which new skills are extracted. These skills, in turn, guide the model's subsequent interactions and parameter updates. As the model's capabilities evolve, previously beneficial skills may become redundant or detrimental. We present SkillDuet, a framework that coordinates parameter updates and skill evolution through model response feedback. Skills extracted from on-policy trajectories guide parameter updates through OPD at every step. A response-based score, Strength, ranks candidate skills by the magnitude of the shift they induce in the current model's responses, and the highest-scoring skills are periodically consolidated into a persistent global skill set (Global). The updated model and Global jointly guide subsequent interactions, generating experience for further parameter and skill updates. With Qwen3-4B, SkillDuet achieves success rates of 98.57% on ALFWorld and 92.97% on WebShop, exceeding the matched SEED-API baseline by 2.86 and 5.47 percentage points, respectively. Ablations show that response-based skill selection and Global consolidation improve task performance. Further experiments show that the benefits of retained skills depend on both their content and their compatibility with the model. SkillDuet provides a concrete mechanism for model-skill co-evolution and skill-level recursive self-improvement.

title: Perils and opportunities of AI for public climate services

payload.title: Perils and opportunities of AI for public climate services
payload.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative and machine-learning systems, in climate services development and provision is transforming how climate information is produced, accessed, and interpreted. AI-enabled climate services offer significant opportunities for process automation, optimisation, tailoring, and the translation of complex climate data into actionable knowledge for diverse users. However, the growing reliance on privately controlled algorithms, data infrastructures, and computing facilities raises critical concerns related to governance, transparency, equity and economic sustainability, among others. While the technical architecture of climate services increasingly relies on advanced machine learning and large-scale climate models, their legitimacy as public services may be weakened in the absence of arrangements that prioritise public value and long-lasting societal benefit over profit maximisation. The tension between the public mandate of climate services and the private nature of AI infrastructure challenges traditional notions of openness. Using a consensus-based elicitation method coupled with the PESTLE framework, we analyse the political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental risks and opportunities shaping the co-production value chain of AI-enabled climate services. We draw policy-relevant conclusions for data, model and infrastructure supporting the next generation of upstream and downstream climate services as critical applications for society. Our work presents potential and plausible challenges and benefits for a pan-European, decentralised public climate service built on sovereign AI infrastructure and open governance principles.

title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path

payload.title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path
payload.abstract: We present a real-time method for reconstructing fully integrated pixel radiance in rendered volumetric media under direct and ambient environmental illumination, using compact, low-cost scene features and statistics. Unlike Monte Carlo denoising pipelines for volumetric rendering, which depend on computationally expensive path-traced radiance estimates, our approach directly infers the final light-transport solution from inexpensive primary-ray and environment sample evaluations. We show that these features form a near-sufficient representation of the scene, enabling accurate reconstruction at substantially lower computational cost. Using an attention-augmented image-to-image network, we demonstrate that complete pixel radiance can be inferred directly from these auxiliary features, without requiring the original radiance signal. Operating in image space also provides a more stable computational cost as the camera zooms into or out of the volume, with substantially less dependence on volume density than approaches based on explicit multiple-scattering simulation. We demonstrate real-time performance and high reconstruction accuracy in challenging volumetric cloud scenarios.

title: FALC: An Artifact-Centric Life Cycle Model and Research Agenda for AI Forensics

payload.title: FALC: An Artifact-Centric Life Cycle Model and Research Agenda for AI Forensics
payload.abstract: AI systems increasingly appear in criminal investigations as tools, targets, and sources of evidence, yet AI forensics lacks a systematic account of the artifacts they produce: investigators often do not know which traces to look for, and for many traces they do find, no established analysis technique exists. In this paper we first developed the Forensic AI Life Cycle (FALC) that unlike other life cycle models shifts the focus onto the forensic artifacts created during the life cycle of an AI system. Through FALC we derived a reference list of artifacts that might serve an investigation. Second, we collected examples for crimes with AI involvement throughout FALC and questions likely to be asked when investigating these crimes. Third, we propose a taxonomy of forensic fields of expertise with a focus on the current possibility to analyze AI forensic artifacts using established techniques. For investigators, the model provides a systematic basis for identifying which artifacts to look for when an AI system is relevant to a case. For researchers, the classification shows where existing forensic methods already suffice and where new techniques are most urgently needed.

title: Calibrating Document-Local Boundaries for Contextual Chunk Retrieval

payload.title: Calibrating Document-Local Boundaries for Contextual Chunk Retrieval
payload.abstract: Late Chunking encodes an entire document before pooling at chunk boundaries, preserving document context in local retrieval units. Chunk-level post-training improves context-dependent retrieval, but shared context can make semantically similar same-document negatives difficult to distinguish. We study the local decision boundary between a gold chunk and its hardest sibling. Starting from InSeNT, we analyze InSeNT's within-document gradients and show that the entropy of the conditional negative allocation decreases monotonically with the scaling factor at fixed logits. We propose a two-part framework for calibrating document-local chunk boundaries. The first component adapts the discriminative scale from within-document margins, while the second exposes chunk partitions to attention during document encoding. Experiments on ConTEB and NanoBEIR show that the resulting model improves contextual chunk retrieval across the evaluated encoder settings while retaining competitive passage-level retrieval quality; ablations further characterize the distinct roles of adaptive scaling and chunk-aware routing.

title: Artifact Filtering versus Artifact-Compensated Training in JPEG to JPEG AI Recompression

payload.title: Artifact Filtering versus Artifact-Compensated Training in JPEG to JPEG AI Recompression
payload.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of recompression of images from JPEG to JPEG AI format. We show that direct recompression from JPEG to JPEG~AI trained on uncompressed images is accompanied by the preservation of the JPEG image artifacts in the resulting JPEG~AI image. In order to avoid it, we evaluate an approach where an artifacts removal neural network is first applied to the input JPEG image as an external pre-filter. However, in this case, the processing time is increased by 29 times. Therefore, we propose an artifact-compensated training for JPEG AI and show that it is able to combine pre-filtering against target distortions with efficient compression without increase in the processing time.

title: CRAFT-AI: Capability and Requirement Alignment for Flexible Manufacturing through Agentic AI

payload.title: CRAFT-AI: Capability and Requirement Alignment for Flexible Manufacturing through Agentic AI
payload.abstract: One of the fundamental needs for reaching resilient production infrastructure is flexible manufacturing, which requires translating changing production requirements into implementable system configurations. This paper introduces \textbf{CRAFT-AI}, an agentic AI approach combining natural language (NL) requirement interpretation, Asset Administration Shell (AAS)-based capability descriptions, and reusable engineering knowledge from existing manufacturing configurations. A tool-using AI agent matches requirements with available capabilities and reference implementations to generate manufacturing scenes and corresponding AAS instances. The approach is demonstrated using a Factory I/O prototype with twelve reference scenes and five illustrative manufacturing tasks of varying complexity, providing an initial feasibility assessment of the proposed AAS-enabled, system-level generative engineering approach. For the four valid user task descriptions, proper requirements, correct references to the relevant engineering knowledge, correct components and lastly a valid Factory I/O scene are generated. For the task with missing engineering knowledge and a wrong sensor selection, the user is informed about which requirements of the scene generation lack domain knowledge and also which sensor is not compatible with the selected raw material by the user with link to the related documentation. After fixing the task description, the correct scene is seamlessly generated. \textbf{CRAFT-AI} highlights the importance of safeguards for risk perception and communication in foundation model-driven solutions.

title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition

payload.title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition
payload.abstract: Wearable Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) enable pervasive Human Activity Recognition (HAR), but traditional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) suffer from an "arithmetic-latency deadlock" due to dense floating-point MAC operations. While Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer ultra-low power, existing ones face spatial blind spots, rigid neurons, and gradient degradation. To address these, we propose TSFFormer, a purely spiking Fourier Transformer for Green HAR. It introduces two key innovations: (1) a MultiHeadFourier attention that performs frequency-domain global mixing, reducing complexity from \(O(V^2)\) to \(O(V\log V)\), eliminating spatial blind spots, and saving \(\sim\)50% GPU memory; and (2) a dual-compartment Temporal Spiking LIF (TSLIFNode) that utilizes dynamic thresholds to adapt to non-stationary rhythms and mitigate gradient degradation. Extensive experiments on 8 public IMU benchmarks demonstrate that TSFFormer surpasses state-of-the-art SNNs and even the classic DeepConvLSTM, achieving a \(\sim\)3\(\times\) faster training speed with an energy footprint of 0.1 pJ. Ablation studies confirm the synergistic effect of our modules, providing a highly accurate, ultra-low-power event-driven paradigm for wearable sensing.

title: Zero-Search Reinforcement Learning for Slay the Spire 2 with Failure-Driven Restarts

payload.title: Zero-Search Reinforcement Learning for Slay the Spire 2 with Failure-Driven Restarts
payload.abstract: Slay the Spire 2 (STS2) is a deck-building roguelike in which a winning run at the highest difficulty takes several hundred decisions, and most losses happen in late boss fights that a learner seldom reaches. We train agents that choose every action with one forward pass of a 6.6M-parameter entity transformer, without lookahead. Training and evaluation run the game's own compiled assembly (v0.107.1) in a headless .NET host. The host replays a run exactly from its seed and actions, so training episodes can restart from states the learner has visited, and a failure-driven curriculum allocates these restarts in proportion to where complete runs are lost. On 12,800 held-out games at Ascension 10 (A10), the released policies win 8.05% averaged over the five characters (Ironclad 15.6%, Regent 12.5%), and AlphaSpire's released networks used without search win 0.55% on a common panel. Longer A10 training raised Ironclad from 12.4% to 15.6% and Defect from 3.0% to 8.1% on these games. At Ascension 0 the released policies win 80.2%, level with the 80.3% that the tree-search agent Spire Mentor reports, while Mentor leads by 5 to 8 points from A4 upward. Run in our host on the same 2,000 A10 games, Mentor's search wins 8.8% against 8.2% for our policies, which need 21-27 ms per decision on one CPU core. GPT-6 Astra at maximum reasoning won none of 11 A10 games through our text interface. In a controlled study of 18 training runs from six random initializations, failure-driven allocation exceeds uniform restart allocation on each of three Regent initializations, by 3.6 percentage points on average, while the Silent effect is small and changes sign. Code, trained policies, an in-game mod and the records behind every table are at https://github.com/HalfVulpes/sts2ai.

title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos

payload.title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos
payload.abstract: Embodied navigation requires agents to achieve persistent spatial awareness and long-horizon execution stability in open-world environments. However, existing navigation architectures struggle to sustain both capabilities, remaining effective only over a handful of recent frames. We present Compass 1, the first embodied navigation foundation model to unify language understanding and video generation while enabling memory backtracking through nearly 2mins of visual history. Without altering the underlying architecture, we introduce History Representation, which integrates sparse visual keyframes with an explicit History Representation Map to preserve long-term spatiotemporal context. To effectively leverage this history, we further introduce History Utilization, a structured VQA supervision protocol comprising three categories: task-stage grounding, exploration consistency, and spatiotemporal target retrieval, enabling map-grounded reasoning and stable persistent long-horizon navigation. To fuel this system, we establish a complete annotation pipeline for monocular RGB videos and open-source a massive dataset featuring over 500 hours of high-quality real-world interactions and over 2,000 hours of annotated web videos. Trained mainly on the distribution of 1m height camera, Compass 1 generalizes seamlessly across diverse embodiments and scenarios, ranging from indoor environments to pedestrian-dense streets, spanning wheeled robot at 0.35m, quadruped dog at 0.5m, humanoid at 0.85m, and aerial drone at 1.5m. Compass 1achieves a dominant overall success rate of 79.4% across open-world evaluations, compared to 17.8% for the strongest baseline. It demonstrates exceptional zero-shot execution exceeding 90% on foundational tasks, a 250% boost in exploration, and an unparalleled leap from 0% to 58% in challenging persistent history backtracking.

title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning

payload.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
payload.abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

title: Correct First, Fast Second: What a Local 7B Code Model Can and Cannot Do for GPU Kernel Optimization

payload.title: Correct First, Fast Second: What a Local 7B Code Model Can and Cannot Do for GPU Kernel Optimization
payload.abstract: We study how much the interaction strategy around a fixed, locally hosted 7B-parameter code model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct) affects its ability to replace PyTorch operators with custom CUDA kernels. On 30 KernelBench tasks (levels 1-3, first 10 each, evaluated on a V100), we compare four regimes of increasing structure: zero-shot prompting, profiling-guided prompting, iterative refinement on execution feedback, and a multi-agent loop (analysis, retrieval, generation, evaluation, feedback triage) in which the same model fills four roles around a non-LLM evaluator. Three findings stand out. (1) Correctness, not speed, is the binding constraint: even correct generated kernels average 0.97-0.99x the speed of eager PyTorch, because a 7B model cannot out-write cuBLAS/cuDNN on dense GEMM and convolution; the only real wins are fused memory-bound epilogues. (2) The best strategy depends on difficulty: profiling-guided prompting is strongest overall (43% correct, 27% faster than baseline), but the agent loop is the only method that solves any level-2 fusion problem (3/10 vs. 0/10 for all others). (3) Naive agentic scaffolding is actively harmful: our first agent scored 3% correct, below zero-shot's 30%, and the decisive repairs were matching the agent's ambition to the model's competence and spending compute on best-of-n sampling under a real execution oracle (3% to 33% correct from n=1 to n=8), not on more reasoning steps.

title: TypedInk: Knowing When Not To Draw

payload.title: TypedInk: Knowing When Not To Draw
payload.abstract: Can a scientific figure generator know when it does not have enough evidence to draw? Complete-source illustrators map a finished methodology section to a schematic, or a table to plotting code, and are never asked this question because their input is assumed complete. The research record is rarely that complete: an outline, a draft paragraph, a table, or a one-sentence intent, in any combination, and painting measured numbers with an image model when the table is missing is a hallucinated result. TypedInk infers a figure type from {diagram, plot, plate} from a possibly incomplete source and dispatches to the renderer that can honor that type's evidence contract, refusing dispatch when the contract cannot be met. On the six gold plots in TypedFigBench (5 views, n=30), TypedInk's code path inks every gold table token when a table is observed (12/12), refuses the 12 hidden-table views instead of inventing numbers, and marks 6 intent-only views illustrative, with no execution failures. An always-draw coder with no such gate inks 30/30 charts, including all 18 with no table, and recovers zero gold numbers on any of them; two vision-language raters (not humans; human replication is future work) still judge those always-draw charts submittable 17/36 times, against TypedInk's refusal 0/36 times. A diagnostic field ablation of the type router (16 illustrations, 5 views each, n=80) locates where this failure would originate if unchecked: an outline alone yields type accuracy 0.31 and sends every gold plot into an integrity violation, and a chat-model planner narrows but does not close the gap (overall accuracy 0.85, still integrity-failing on 25% of outlines). Diagram-label recall is 0.47 on the full record and 0.19 on an outline. Gold plates are typed at dispatch (oracle integrity-fail 0.00) and rendered as stills.

title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication

payload.title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication
payload.abstract: Remote face authentication requires protection against both presentation attacks and biometric data injection attacks prior to face matching. Methods based on active screen illumination appear promising for both by introducing randomized visual stimuli through the user's device screen and evaluating the corresponding facial responses. Although such methods have been more studied for presentation attack detection (PAD), their systematic evaluation for injection attack detection (IAD) remains limited. To address this gap, we first classify injected content into static images, prerecorded videos, and real-time deepfakes based on their expected responses to the challenge. We then adapt an active screen-illumination approach into an implementation we term color wave and develop a systematic, injection-specific evaluation protocol. The protocol examines detection effectiveness, generalization across operating conditions, robustness to signal degradation, and susceptibility to selected evasion strategies. The findings demonstrate a strong discriminative signal under controlled conditions but also reveal performance limitations under overexposure, low screen brightness, and subject motion, as well as vulnerabilities to selected evasion strategies. By relating detection outcomes to attack types and operating conditions, this study provides an interpretable assessment of when and why active screen illumination succeeds or fails as an IAD mechanism.

title: XposedMIA: Exploiting Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for One-Shot Membership Inference Attacks

payload.title: XposedMIA: Exploiting Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for One-Shot Membership Inference Attacks
payload.abstract: Machine learning (ML) services increasingly expose explainability outputs alongside model predictions. While such explanations are intended to improve transparency, they may also reveal information about the underlying training data. In this work, we show that the local surrogate geometry employed by Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) can be repurposed as a proxy for a sample's distance to the model's decision boundary. We extend this boundary-distance view to tabular counterfactual explanations and, for the first time, to visual counterfactual explanations for image classifiers. We present XposedMIA, a one-shot, explanation-based black-box membership inference attack (MIA) framework that converts the returned explanation into a proxy for the queried sample's distance to the model decision boundary. After a one-time calibration step on a small labeled calibration set of as few as 30 samples, our attack requires only a single query for each target sample. Unlike prior label-only attacks requiring iterative queries or shadow training, our method relies solely on the predicted label and its accompanying explanation. Our evaluation indicates that XposedMIA achieves high effectiveness, with success rates of up to 0.95 using only a single query per target, revealing that releasing explanations introduces an additional channel for membership leakage.

title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers

payload.title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers
payload.abstract: A model that takes over another model's conversation must normally re-read the whole history; a text hand-off shortens the re-read only by dropping content. KV-cache translation instead maps the source's cache into the target's own format, so the target continues from the full context without re-reading it. It works for grouped-query attention (GQA), but open-weights frontier models now cache compressed latents (MLA), sparse-attention indexer keys and fixed-size linear-attention states. We replicate KV-Lingo on a GQA pair and then give, for each of these objects, where to capture and inject it and a mechanism that reaches native quality. We study two hybrid pairs at 16-48B scale in both directions, Kimi-VL-A3B - Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA - MLA + Kimi Delta Attention) and Qwen3.5-27B - Qwen3.8-27B (Gated DeltaNet hybrids), plus a sparse-attention target (Qwen3.8-27B - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). MLA latents translate with token-wise linear maps; recurrent states are copied with a closed-form correction or synthesised by replaying the target's own recurrence. Exact long-range recall needs token identity: decoding token ids from the source's layer-0 MLA latent raises needle recall from 0.09 to 0.99 at 2-32K and to 0.83-1.00 at 64K, eight times the longest training prompt. The hybrid full-MLA direction is within the paired confidence interval of native quality on every task metric, and same-shape GDN hybrids reach the native level in both directions (apart from 6% refusals inherited from the source), with time to first token 18.7 and 46.8 times shorter than a re-read at 64K tokens. Segment-wise multi-turn transfer stays at the re-prefill level; naive re-translation collapses. On the sparse-attention target, predicted indexer keys recall the needle as well as the target's own keys (one seed). We state as a hypothesis how the recipes transfer to 300B+ hybrid flagships.

title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching

payload.title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
payload.abstract: We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.

title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling

payload.title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
payload.abstract: Large language models offer a promising technique for translating natural-language optimization problems into solver code, but their reliability remains constrained by the quality of template retrieval. While recent structured methods improve over flat prompting through hierarchical taxonomy search, their traversal rules remain fixed or LLM-driven at inference time, leaving retrieval unable to improve from past successes and failures. This motivates treating template retrieval as a policy that can be learned from modeling experience, rather than as a static inference-time rule. We propose COMPASS, a policy-amortized framework for retrieving optimization templates in LLM-based solver modeling, which represents the template library as a directed acyclic graph and formulates retrieval as a sequential decision process over template nodes. A deep Q-network learns a reusable traversal policy from template-level judgments and execution feedback, reducing reliance on fixed heuristic traversal through feedback-driven graph navigation. To support extensible retrieval, COMPASS embeds problem descriptions and template nodes in a shared semantic space, allowing newly inserted templates to be scored from their text descriptions without redefining the action space. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and optimization-modeling benchmarks demonstrate that COMPASS consistently improves over heuristic structured retrieval, with the largest gains on complex and mixed-category problems.

title: Exact Natarajan Dimension of Homogeneous Multiclass Linear Predictors

payload.title: Exact Natarajan Dimension of Homogeneous Multiclass Linear Predictors
payload.abstract: The Natarajan dimension is a fundamental measure of the capacity of multiclass hypothesis classes and plays an important role in analyzing their generalization ability. In this paper, by establishing lower and upper bounds, we show that the exact Natarajan dimension of homogeneous multiclass linear predictors with pairwise distinct class weights is \(n(k-1)-1\), where $n$ is the dimension of the feature space and $k$ is the number of classes, for \(n,k\ge3\), \(n,k\in\mathbb N\).

title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development

payload.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
payload.abstract: Coding agents increasingly receive UI screenshots as part of bug reports, yet degraded image quality - caused by low resolution, compression artifacts, or small rendered text - can prevent them from identifying the relevant UI elements and source files. Vision-language models become less reliable as image quality deteriorates, while OCR-assisted approaches may propagate recognition errors from degraded inputs. Both approaches are limited when the visual evidence required for localization is no longer clearly observable in the query screenshot. We propose augmenting coding agents with repository-rendered reference images: crisp screenshots generated from the same codebase that the agent is tasked with modifying. These references provide readable visual evidence of the application's UI while preserving the current, potentially bug-containing implementation state. Because they are generated from the available repository rather than requiring a known bug-free version, they can be produced automatically for reproducible application states without manual image annotation. We evaluate the approach on a controlled benchmark derived from SWE-bench Multimodal by injecting visual UI bugs into a real web application. We vary screenshot degradation and reference-image provision and measure whether the coding agent identifies the correct source file. The results show that reference images improve file localization especially for degraded image quality, increasing the gold file match rate under fourfold downsampling with JPEG compression. We confirmed with further analysis that the proposed approach recognizes text approximately 12 percentage points better than language biased OCR under the same degradation.

title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes

payload.title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
payload.abstract: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets

payload.title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets
payload.abstract: Constrained preference-conditioned MORL typically assumes full task observability, treating preferences and safety budgets as stationary task signals. In real-world deployment, however, these signals are often unreliable proxies: intent may drift, safety tolerances may shift with context, and exposed descriptors may be noisy, delayed, or incomplete. We therefore formulate constrained preference-conditioned MORL as a partially observed task-specification problem, where the agent must navigate a fundamental conflict between unreliable external signals and latent interaction dynamics. We propose \textbf{BECON}, a belief-conditioned framework for constrained MORL with drifting preferences and budgets, which infers latent task context from recent histories to estimate preferences and safety budgets.
